subject: Cognitive Science
title: Concrete Operations
description: A micro-lesson that makes Concrete Operations usable.

hook.text: Ask an eight-year-old the water question. "Same water, different glass." She nails it now.

buildup.text: Concrete operations (ages seven to eleven) bring logical thinking about real, tangible things.

discovery.text: Children master reversibility, seriation, and classification—they can order and group.

twist.text: But ask "What if gravity reversed?" and she struggles. Hypothetical reasoning isn't here yet.

climax.text: This stage aligns with school entry: kids can now handle math, science, and systematic rules.

punchline.text: Logic arrives, but only for the real world.

quiz.question: What can children in the concrete operational stage do?
